- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then gradually decline — suggesting a lag in recognizing mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike, forecasts often overcorrect downward, missing the true continuation or reversal.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history shows volatility or upward momentum.
- Forecasts are less accurate when true outcomes show strong downward momentum or sudden drops — model fails to adjust quickly.
- Model underestimates when true prices are near or below recent 7–10 day moving averages — suggests failure to recognize mean reversion.
- Forecasts are more accurate when true prices are near historical 30-day average — model is better calibrated to stable periods.
- Model tends to ignore short-term volatility and overweights long-term trends — leading to overconfidence in trend continuation.
- Forecasts often fail to account for policy or market intervention events — e.g., emission caps, auction changes — which cause sudden price shifts.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher prices in the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon — should be adjusted downward if recent history shows downward momentum.
